extraction.name: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images
extraction.description: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.citeAs: Mathew et al., DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images, arXiv:2007.00398v3, 2021
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Pages were hand-picked from these documents. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in three stages: initial question-answer pair definition, verification by a different worker, and review by authors for mismatches.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning 6,071 documents from 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) from 1900 to 2018.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were selected to minimize binarized images to avoid poor image quality. Pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures were prioritized. Questions were filtered if they were found to be inapt due to language issues or ambiguity. Data was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio for train, validation, and test.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages. Stage 1: Remote workers defined up to 10 question-answer pairs per image, entering answers verbatim. Stage 2: A different worker verified answers and assigned question types, flagging inapt questions. Stage 3: Authors reviewed cases where stage 1 and stage 2 answers did not match, editing or accepting/rejecting questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were tagged with one or more of 9 question types (handwritten, form, layout, table/list, running text, photograph, figure, yes/no, other) during the second stage to analyze reasoning requirements.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers and volunteers from the authors' institution
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to inspire a 'purpose-driven' point of view in Document Analysis and Recognition (DAR) research, moving beyond simple information extraction to holistic document understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is drawn from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, which may introduce biases related to the specific industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) and time periods represented. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing models perform reasonably well but have a large performance gap compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy). Models struggle specifically with questions requiring understanding of document structure, figures, and diagrams. OCR errors can impact performance. The dataset contains a high density of semantic information and varied document types.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation of Visual Question Answering (VQA) models on document images. Baseline evaluation for Document Visual Question Answering tasks.
